public_rationale: The September 30, 2024 report put OpenAI's expected full-year 2024 loss at $5 billion, excluding equity-based compensation [e1]. The June 16, 2026 report put its full-year 2024 net loss just above $5 billion, but did not reconcile that figure to the earlier estimate's accounting basis [e2]. The evidence therefore does not establish whether the realized 2024 loss exceeded $5 billion on the required comparable basis [e1, e2].
limitations: The rounded forecast in e1 establishes neither a realized loss nor a strict exceedance of $5 billion.
The reported net loss in e2 does not establish a result above or below the threshold after applying the original estimate's equity-compensation exclusion and other material adjustments.

public_payload.normalized_proposition: OpenAI is on course to lose more than $5 billion in 2024.

statement.excerpt: OpenAI, the biggest player in the industry, is on course to lose more than $5 billion this year, with competitor Anthropic (which also makes its own transformer-based model, Claude) on course to lose more than $2.7 billion this year.

our_interpretation: 'This year' means calendar 2024, and 'more than' requires a result strictly above $5 billion.
I assess the eventual annual result, rather than merely whether a forecast existed when Zitron wrote.

The surrounding discussion relies on reported financial estimates. Contemporary reporting describes the approximately $5 billion forecast as excluding equity-based compensation; that basis must be preserved when comparing it with an outcome.
The words 'lose' and 'net loss' do not by themselves establish that a later GAAP result is comparable to the original adjusted estimate.
criteria.support_condition: An independently established full-year 2024 loss exceeds $5 billion on the same basis as the contemporaneous estimate.
criteria.contradiction_condition: An independently established full-year 2024 loss is $5 billion or less on that same basis.

evidence.locator: Paragraph beginning 'But OpenAI sees a loss'
evidence.explanation: This identifies an important adjustment in the contemporaneous full-year forecast. It reports an expectation, so it cannot establish the final result or a strict exceedance.

evidence.locator: Section 'Gotta spend money to make money', opening sentence
evidence.explanation: The article reports a 2024 net loss above the numerical threshold from audited statements and says the Financial Times reviewed the documents. It does not reconcile this result to the earlier loss estimate excluding equity compensation; it also identifies Zitron as the original recipient of the documents.

public_payload.what_would_resolve: Company records or independent financial reporting establishing the final full-year 2024 loss, reconciled to the original estimate's exclusion of equity-based compensation and other material adjustments, with enough precision to determine whether it exceeded $5 billion.
